name: CUDA-Q
description: CUDA-Q (formerly CUDA Quantum) is NVIDIA's open-source platform for hybrid quantum-classical computing. It enables developers to integrate quantum processing units (QPUs) with GPUs and CPUs for high-performance quantum simulations and algorithm development. CUDA-Q supports both Python and C++.

news.title: Pasqal Integrates NVIDIA CUDA-Q with QRMI for Slurm-Native Hybrid HPC-Quantum Workflows
news.excerpt: Pasqal announced integration of NVIDIA CUDA-Q platform with its Quantum Resource Management Interface (QRMI) runtime, enabling CUDA-Q workloads to be scheduled through Slurm-based HPC workflows.

news.title: Quantum X Labs Tests AI-Based Error Correction Decoder With NVIDIA CUDA-Q Tools
news.excerpt: Quantum X Labs reported progress on AI-driven quantum error-correction program using NVIDIA CUDA-Q QEC software libraries, benchmarking transformer-based decoder against classical MWPM decoder.

news.title: Harnessing CUDA-Q's MPS for Tensor Network Simulations of Large-Scale Quantum Circuits
news.excerpt: Research paper evaluating CUDA-Q tensor network simulators on an Nvidia Grace Hopper system, particularly the Matrix Product State (MPS) formulation. Submitted to 33rd Euromicro International Conference on Parallel, Distributed and Network-Based Processing (PDP 2025).

news.title: CUDA-Q 0.15.0 released with QEC decoder primitives, LLVM 22 upgrade, and Python 3.13 support
news.excerpt: CUDA-Q 0.15.0 adds source-language support for detector, logical_observable, and detectors primitives for quantum error correction, upgrades LLVM from version 16 to 22.1, and adds CUDA 13 and Python 3.13 support. Enables real-time QEC decoding on Quantinuum backends and job submission to QCI backends.

news.title: NVIDIA Introduces NVQLink — Open Architecture Connecting QPUs to GPUs, Supporting 17 Quantum Hardware Builders
news.excerpt: NVIDIA announced NVQLink on July 27, 2026: an open system architecture for tightly coupling quantum processors to GPU-based HPC clusters via high-speed, low-latency (microsecond) interconnect. NVQLink supports 17 QPU builders, 5 controller builders, and 9 US national laboratories within the CUDA-Q ecosystem.

news.title: CUDA-Q 0.15.1 released
news.excerpt: NVIDIA released CUDA-Q 0.15.1, a patch update to the hybrid quantum-classical computing platform with bug fixes and improvements to simulation backends.

news.title: CUDA-Q 0.16.0 released with Python 3.14 support, disconnected topologies, and static Rotation Gate Synthesis
news.excerpt: CUDA-Q version 0.16.0 was released on September 12, 2026. Key additions include support for disconnected device topologies in the qubit mapper, Python 3.14 support, expanded mapping support for control flow, static Rotation Gate Synthesis (Clifford + T), and introduction of atomic quantum regions.

news.title: Quantum Machines Demonstrates Live End-to-End CUDA-Q Program Execution via NVIDIA NVQLink
news.excerpt: Quantum Machines became the first quantum control company to run a complete end-to-end NVIDIA CUDA-Q program across live qubits and a classical PPU processor using NVIDIA NVQLink, announced at IEEE Quantum Week 2026. A single CUDA-Q program routes quantum and classical tasks to appropriate processors, exchanging measurements and control decisions in microseconds.

news.title: NVIDIA Launches CUDA-Q Logical: Open-Source Framework for Fault-Tolerant Quantum Computing
news.excerpt: NVIDIA introduced CUDA-Q Logical on September 14, 2026 — an open-source compiler orchestration layer that maps logical quantum programs onto error-correcting codes. Fermilab cut fault-tolerant architecture evaluation from five months to three weeks. Iceberg Quantum modelled 1,000 logical qubits with only 150,000 physical qubits. Early adopters include Fermilab, Infleqtion, IQM, QCDesign, Quantum Motion, and Sandia National Laboratories.
